name: Allopurinol
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Allopurinol and its active metabolite oxipurinol are cleared by the kidneys, so exposure rises steeply as kidney function falls. The US label gives starting doses by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) for gout, then slow titration by 50 mg/day every 2 to 4 weeks.
kidney_function_basis: Label tables use eGFR in mL/min (gout table) and mL/min (cancer-therapy table); not indexed to 1.73 m2 in the label text.

bands.recommendation: Gout: no starting-dose modification (label: eGFR >60 mL/min). Titrate to serum urate target; use the lowest effective dose.
Gout: start 50 mg daily (label: eGFR >30 to 60 mL/min); increase by 50 mg/day every 2 to 4 weeks. Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia: no modification at eGFR >20 to 60 mL/min.
bands.short: Gout: 50 mg/d start; +50 mg q2–4 wk

bands.recommendation: Gout: start 50 mg every other day (label: eGFR >15 to 30 mL/min); titrate slowly. Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia: 200 mg/day at eGFR 10 to 20 mL/min.
bands.short: Gout: 50 mg every other day start

bands.recommendation: Gout: start 50 mg twice weekly (eGFR 5 to 15 mL/min) or 50 mg once weekly (eGFR <5 mL/min). Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia: 100 mg/day at eGFR <10 mL/min.

hd.text: Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia on dialysis: 50 mg every 12 hours or 100 mg every 24 hours (label). The label gives no gout-specific dialysis dose; maximum doses by eGFR are not defined.
hd.short: No gout dose; cancer use 100 mg q24h

pd.text: No PD-specific dose in the label; the label's 'on dialysis' row (cancer-therapy hyperuricemia) does not name the modality.

crrt.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: use with specialist input.

dialyzable: Yes: allopurinol and oxipurinol are dialyzable (label, Overdosage); benefit of dialysis in overdose is unknown.
monitoring: Monitor kidney function closely when starting in chronic kidney disease (CKD); reduce or stop if kidney abnormalities appear and persist. Watch for serious skin reactions.

pediatric.approved_ages: Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia: established in pediatric patients (about 200 studied). Not established for gout, recurrent calcium oxalate calculi, or inborn errors of purine metabolism.
pediatric.usual_dose: Cancer-therapy hyperuricemia: 100 mg/m2 orally every 8 to 12 hours (10 mg/kg/day), maximum 800 mg/day; keep urine output at least 100 mL/m2/hour.

renal.recommendation: Insufficient information in the label to set pediatric doses in kidney impairment; weigh risks and benefits (label). Specialist input.
Insufficient information in the label to set pediatric doses in kidney impairment; weigh risks and benefits (label). Specialist input.

hd.text: Not studied in children on dialysis (label). Specialist input.

pd.text: Not studied in children on dialysis (label). Specialist input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonates: specialist input (label gives no neonatal dose).
pediatric.notes: The label states treatment has not been studied in pediatric patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR <20 mL/min) or on dialysis.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Selected US label is the Rising Pharma ANDA-style label on NDA016084 (2026 version), which uses eGFR tables; older Zyloprim labels used CrCl-based reductions. Confirm the PH package insert wording.
Label band edges (>60, >30–60, >15–30, 5–15, <5) do not map exactly onto our ≥60/30–59/15–29/<15 bands; edges kept verbatim inside the text.
Gout dosing in dialysis is not given by the label; only the cancer-therapy table has an 'on dialysis' row. Decide whether to show it for gout.
Maximum dose by eGFR is explicitly 'not defined' in the label; treat-to-target titration above the starting dose is a clinical judgment call.
pediatric: Only cancer-therapy hyperuricemia is an established pediatric indication; mg/kg (10 mg/kg/day) and mg/m2 both appear in the label.
No pediatric renal adjustment is given; all pediatric kidney bands are 'specialist input'.
